Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Investments Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Investments' second quarter results. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Laura Patel, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter of 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust assets under management growth to $1.25 trillion, reflecting our diversified strategies across equities, fixed income, alternatives, and ESG products, amid favorable market conditions and strong client inflows.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Investments delivered strong results in the second quarter. Our revenue was $4.2 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by the direct linkage between our AUM expansion and fee-based revenue model, where management fees make up the bulk of our top line. Our expenses were $2.8 billion, resulting in net income of $1.2 billion. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in key growth initiatives.

Let me expand on our assets under management, which remains the cornerstone of our franchise. Ending AUM reached $1.25 trillion as of quarter-end, reflecting 9.2% quarter-over-quarter growth and a robust 18.5% year-over-year increase. This was powered by $28 billion in net inflows—our strongest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021—and market appreciation contributing approximately $85 billion, fueled by the rally in U.S. large-cap equities with mid-teens S&P 500 returns, plus gains in European peripherals and Asian tech. Organic growth, stripping out market moves and FX, was 2.1%, highlighting the strength of our client relationships and product appeal. This AUM momentum directly boosted fee revenue by 12% year-over-year, aided by a modest 3 basis point expansion in our blended fee rate to 152 basis points, thanks to higher-margin alternatives now at 22% of total AUM, up from 18% last year.

Geographically, this underscores our balanced global presence. North America is 52% of AUM, or $650 billion, up 11% quarter-over-quarter and 22% year-over-year. It remains our core growth driver, with $15 billion in net retail inflows into low-cost ETFs like our Apex S&P 500 Core ETF, which attracted $4.2 billion amid the AI boom. Institutional defined contribution plans added $6 billion into target-date funds, driven by record 401(k) contributions, while market gains from Nasdaq and S&P contributed $45 billion. We're advancing with our Apex Retirement AI platform, using machine learning for personalized glide paths, which has lifted retention 15% in pilots.

Europe holds 27% of AUM at $337.5 billion, with 7.8% QoQ and 14% YoY growth. Net inflows hit $8.5 billion, led by €5 billion into sustainable strategies under EU SFDR rules and the green bond rally. Our Apex Eurozone ESG Equity Fund beat the MSCI Europe SRI by 250 basis points, drawing Nordic pension mandates. UK AUM was flat from sterling-hedged outflows amid BOE volatility, but DACH expansion via UBS-like private bank partnerships added €2 billion. Project Horizon, our blockchain fund admin platform, cuts settlement by 40% and secured two German insurer wins.

Asia-Pacific is 16% or $200 billion, fastest-growing at 12.5% QoQ and 28% YoY, with $4.2 billion inflows. Greater China led with $3.1 billion into our QDII Apex China Tech ETF on CSI 300 recovery and stimulus. India added $1.2 billion via EPFO into emerging markets funds during RBI easing, and Japan saw GPIF alt rebalancing. Our Shanghai JV enables RMB hedging, and Shariah products target Malaysia and Indonesia. We're pacing for 20% APAC growth in FY24, with 50 new hires in Singapore and Mumbai.

Rest of World is 5% or $62.5 billion, up 6% QoQ, including $1.5 billion from Brazilian pensions into LatAm infra debt and Gulf inflows into private equity under Vision 2030.

Turning to the revenue impact of these AUM changes, our model is predominantly fee-based, with management fees at 85% of revenue, based on average daily AUM. Our blended fee rate was 42 basis points this quarter, down slightly from 44 bps last year due to ETF and index mix shifts, akin to Vanguard and BlackRock trends. Average AUM rose 7.2% to $1.20 trillion, translating to management fee revenue of $2.82 billion, up 7.9% QoQ and 11.4% YoY—a near-direct passthrough.

Breaking down AUM drivers: markets added $65 billion or 5.7%, with equities up 9.1% to $620 billion on S&P gains and our active strategies outperforming by 120 bps. Fixed income at $312 billion grew 2.6% or $8 billion as yields stabilized, supporting our short-duration ESG ladders. Alternatives at $225 billion held steady with private credit spreads at 450 bps over SOFR.

Net new money added $28 billion or 2.4%, with inflows of $42 billion against $14 billion outflows. RIAs drove $18 billion into passive ETFs, retail target-dates $15 billion on boomer shifts, and institutions $9 billion including a $4 billion PE commitment. FX deducted $8 billion from euro weakness.

Regionally, Americas at 62% or $775 billion grew 10.2%, fueling 70% fee growth at 55 bps. EMEA $275 billion was flat on outflows but stabilizing with Luxembourg feeders. APAC $200 billion up 6.8% on $10 billion ASEAN ETF inflows.

Strategically, new active ETFs like Apex Climate Transition, AI Innovators, and Short Duration Credit drew $8 billion at 38 bps. ApexOne platform boosted RIA retention to 98% with AI analytics, and alts grew 14% YoY with $450 million performance fees.

Now, on net flows by channel, we posted record $28.4 billion inflows, up 15% QoQ and 32% YoY, for 2.1% organic long-term AUM growth beating peers. Fee rate steady at 42 bps, markets added $65 billion from tech equities.

Institutional: $17.2 billion or 60%, up 18% QoQ, channel AUM $795 billion or 55%. U.S. pensions $4.5 billion into Core Plus Bond outperforming by 120 bps. EMEA $7.7 billion from UK LGPS and Dutch transitions, APAC $3.8 billion via EM debt. SMAs up 25% to $6.3 billion. Aladdin ESG tools won $2.8 billion infra mandate. Expect $14-16 billion Q3.

Retail: $9.1 billion or 32%, AUM $520 billion or 36%. ETFs $4.8 billion led by Tech Innovators beating Nasdaq by 450 bps YTD. Target-dates $3.2 billion vs. Vanguard. U.S. 68%, EMEA ECB optimism, APAC platforms. AI app up conversions 22%. Target $40 billion annually.

Alternatives: $2.1 billion or 8%, record high, AUM $135 billion or 9%. Private credit $1.2 billion, Direct Lending V $8.5 billion at LIBOR+550 bps. Hedge $500 million quant, real assets $400 million renewables. U.S. 52%, EMEA AIFMD feeders. New evergreen credit ETF Q1 2025. Guide $10-12 billion FY.

Finally, on operating margin trends, we hit 36.4%, up 420 bps YoY from 32.0% and 110 bps QoQ from 35.3%—top-tier vs. peers like BlackRock and T. Rowe, above 28% industry average.

Revenues up 14% to $1.82 billion on 11% average AUM growth to $1.7 trillion from markets and $28 billion inflows. Passives 58% AUM at 12 bps, alts 22% revenue growth at 45%+ margins. Active equity fees to 38 bps.

Expenses up 8% to $1.16 billion: comp 28.5% flat with deferrals, G&A 14% via $45 million procurement savings. Apex Digital Horizon automated 65% ops, cutting unit costs 18% to $0.42 per $B AUM. AlphaGen saved 22% research, robo-advisory added 150 bps.

Americas 40.1% margins on pensions and ETFs, EMEA 28.7% hit by MiFID but ESG up 25%. APAC 37.5% on China and privates.

Barbell strategy: scale passives, premium alts. FY23 guide 35.5-36.5%, FY24 37-39% on $1.9T AUM.

Laura Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing diversified allocations, hedging overlays in a 60/40 equity/fixed mix, and leaning into thematic opportunities like AI, climate transition, and private credit, which have outperformed benchmarks and attracted flows across channels.

Sarah Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes product innovation like our Q4 active ETF suite with $10 billion seed, client analytics for 5-7% organic flows, M&A with $500 million for alts bolt-ons, tech like blockchain NAV and AI personalization, and targeting $100-110 billion full-year flows for 8-9% organic AUM growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the geographic breakdown of AUM growth and how you're positioning for APAC acceleration?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, John. Michael can provide the color.

Michael Chen: Absolutely, John. As I detailed, North America at 52% grew 11% QoQ on retail ETFs and DC plans, Europe 27% on ESG despite UK flatness via DACH blockchain wins, APAC 16% fastest at 12.5% with China Tech ETF and India EPFO, ROW 5% on LatAm and Gulf. For APAC, Shanghai JV, Shariah launches, and 50 hires set us for 20% FY24 growth, resilient to geo-risks.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on how AUM changes flowed through to revenue amid fee compression?

Michael Chen: Good question. The 8.6% QoQ AUM rise to $1.25T drove 7.9% fee revenue growth via 7.2% average AUM, near one-for-one despite 2 bps compression to 42 bps from ETF mix. Markets 5.7%, flows 2.4% offset FX; alts and new ETFs like AI Innovators provide elasticity for 8-10% revenue growth ahead.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morningstar.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex S&P 500 Core ETF?

Laura Patel: Thanks, Emily. Our Apex S&P 500 Core ETF has been a standout, gathering $4.2 billion in net inflows this quarter amid AI-driven large-cap strength. It tracks the index tightly with 3 bps fees, benefiting from S&P mid-teens returns, high liquidity, and our retirement AI integration boosting adoption in 401(k)s. YTD, it's captured share from peers, contributing to our passive scale at 45% AUM.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Investments. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
